syscalls.comment: Deny process tracing — prevents agents attaching to other processes (container escape vector)
Deny filesystem mount operations
Deny device node creation — prevents /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, raw disk access
Deny kernel module loading/unloading — prevents arbitrary kernel code insertion
Deny kernel replacement via kexec
Deny pivot_root — classic container escape technique
Deny chroot — prerequisite step for classic container escape; the orchestrator has no legitimate use for this syscall
Deny namespace creation via unshare — used in user namespace privilege escalation
Deny joining existing namespaces — prevents escaping to host network/mount namespace

Deny clone() calls requesting any new namespace. Mask 0x7E020000 is CLONE_NEWNS|CLONE_NEWUTS|CLONE_NEWIPC|CLONE_NEWUSER|CLONE_NEWPID|CLONE_NEWNET combined. Normal thread/process clone() is unaffected (Python asyncio subprocess works).
Deny clone3 unconditionally — Linux 5.3+ equivalent of clone. Python 3.11 subprocess falls back to clone() when clone3 returns ENOSYS (errnoRet 38), so this is safe.
Deny perf events — side-channel risk (Spectre/Meltdown class attacks)
Deny kernel keyring access — prevents credential theft from keyring
Deny eBPF program loading — can read arbitrary kernel memory, intercept syscalls
Deny userfaultfd — used in certain use-after-free kernel exploits
Deny kernel syslog (dmesg) access — may contain sensitive host information
Deny cross-process memory read/write — analogous to ptrace for data access; closes the gap where ptrace is denied but process_vm_* is not
Deny anonymous in-memory file creation — used to construct fileless payloads; not required by Python 3.11 asyncio
Deny System V shared memory — prevents inter-container communication via shared kernel IPC namespace; Python asyncio does not use SysV IPC
Deny System V semaphores — not used by Python asyncio; eliminates cross-container IPC attack surface
Deny System V message queues — not used by Python asyncio; eliminates cross-container IPC attack surface
Deny fanotify filesystem event monitoring — prevents observing host-level file access patterns through the shared kernel subsystem
Deny AF_NETLINK sockets (family=16) — prevents reading host routing tables and interface info; normal TCP/UDP (AF_INET=2, AF_INET6=10) are unaffected
Deny AF_PACKET raw sockets (family=17) — prevents bypassing iptables FORWARD rules by sending layer-2 frames directly; CAP_NET_RAW is already dropped, this adds defence-in-depth

Deny open_by_handle_at — exploited in CVE-2019-5736 (runc container escape) to re-open /proc/self/exe and overwrite the host runc binary. Python orchestrator has no legitimate use for file handles obtained via name_to_handle_at.
Deny name_to_handle_at — prerequisite to open_by_handle_at; denying both closes the CVE-2019-5736 / Leaky Vessels class of container escape.

Deny io_uring — multiple privilege escalation CVEs (CVE-2022-29582, CVE-2023-2598, CVE-2024-0582) exist in the io_uring subsystem. Python 3.11 asyncio does not use io_uring; the event loop falls back to epoll transparently.
